bot.list.doc: Every bot, with its state and settings.

bot.get.doc: One bot, with its state and settings.

bot.setUserLayer.doc: Sets or clears fields of a bot's user layer; a change to its instructions applies at its next turn.

bots.pause.doc: The core switch that pauses every bot and routine at once (§9.2).

session.list.doc: Every session: bots' conversations, side threads, background agents and coding sessions (`ListAgents`).

session.attach.doc: Follows a session live: replays events after `since`, then streams them with the inherited `event` notification.

session.history.doc: A page of a session's past events, newest last; sealed card fields never reach a plugin (§5.4).

session.diff.doc: A coding session's or an agent's changes in its folder, read only: the working tree against HEAD (untracked files as added), per file with its hunks, bounded per file and in total. A folder that isn't a git repository, or isn't on this computer, answers no files and a notice. A plugin's own connection (a layer) also needs the capability files, since the diff carries file contents.

session.outputs.doc: The files a session delivered to its outputs folder (`<home>/outputs/<session>`), newest first: names and kinds only, never their content.

session.context.doc: How full a session's context is: its last turn's measured prompt (`turn_completed.contextTokens`, for an agent the context it reported) against its model's context window; `{ reported: false }` for a coding session or an agent whose agent has reported none; null when neither is known.

session.connectors.doc: How many plugin MCP servers a session gets, and how many of them belong to a plugin with a sign-in that isn't signed in: counts only.

session.send.doc: The user's message: it interrupts a bot's main conversation at once; it needs a live connection to the computer running the bot (`BOT_ASLEEP`).

session.resend.doc: Try again on a bot's main conversation whose latest turn ended in an error: the host sends the message that began that turn again, as a new message from this client, when that message was the user's own (a relay another computer's device did not sign, a task notification, a routine, a plugin, a bot or an agent is refused), nothing was sent or started since, and it carries no file and no picture it no longer holds (a picture is checked as the composer's send checks it; a message with files is refused: send it again from the composer). Once per failed turn. The caller names only the session: never the words, a message id or attachments. Not for a side thread, an agent or a coding session, nor for a conversation another computer runs. App role only: it is the app's "Try again" button; the terminal and a phone have none.

session.post.doc: A plugin adds a note, or sends a bot a message that folds in; a turn it starts is the plugin's (§5.4).

session.interrupt.doc: Stops the current step; background tasks keep running (§6.4).

session.stop.doc: Stops a side thread, a background agent or a coding session (`TaskStop`).

session.answer.doc: Answers an `AskUserQuestion`, which plugins may read and show in any form (§5.5).

session.setModel.doc: Switches an agent's or coding session's model mid-session; a bot's model is its user layer (§6.3).

session.stageImage.doc: Stages an image for a session's next message, on the computer that holds it, with the app's caps (§6.6 "attachments"): the media types the bytes must sniff as, and the size. `session.send` names it by the path given back; a client off this computer (a phone, lane I) names only images staged so, never a file of its own.

models.list.doc: The models a session can switch to (`session.setModel`), read-only, for a model picker (lane I's phone among them): every model of a provider plugin that is on, signed in or not, less blocked rows and the rows of a blocked provider (a picker never offers what `session.setModel` refuses). With `session`, only the ones that session's runtime takes. `default` is the user's default model.

models.setDefault.doc: Sets the person's default model (what a bot or a session with no model of its own runs on): a model `models.list` offers whose provider the person added. Kept until they pick another or remove its provider (the setup guide, 2026-11-20).

setup.state.doc: Whether this home is set up for a first working reply: the providers added, the default model and what is missing. The apps' setup guide opens by itself while it isn't, unless dismissed.

setup.dismiss.doc: The person skipped the setup guide (`dismissed: true`: it no longer opens by itself, in either app), or asked for it back.

session.compact.doc: Compacts now: the conversation becomes a summary and the prompt's harness blocks are rebuilt (a cache miss). A conversation inside the compaction's retention window is refused as having nothing to compact; an instructions edit doesn't need it, since it reaches the next turn (§5.6).

memory.list.doc: A bot's memory files: `MEMORY.md` and the files it links to (§6.5).

routine.runNow.doc: Runs a routine now, in a side thread on its computer.

routine.get.doc: One routine of the bot on this computer with its instructions, read from its file as it is now, for the person's edit (`routine.edit`), so an edit never writes over text the person couldn't see. The person's window only.

routine.edit.doc: The user changes a routine on this computer: the core rewrites that routine's own file (§7, the file stays the truth) under the Routine tool's rules: a schedule that doesn't read is refused, its id and webhook key stay where they are, a new name renames its file in the bot's own folder and can't take another routine's name, and a raised level waits for its OK again. The person's window only.

routine.webhookKey.doc: A webhook routine's URL and key, for the user to paste into the service that calls it (§7). The key is shown once; after that only a new one (`rotate`), which replaces it, is shown. Never to a bot, a plugin or a remote client.

archive.list.doc: The previous app's sessions, newest first, for the archive view (§14.1).

archive.history.doc: A previous-app session's transcript, read-only; it never becomes a bot's history.

setup_changed.doc: What the home's setup needs changed: a provider was added or removed, or the default model or the guide's dismissal changed.

bot_changed.doc: A bot's settings or state changed.

bot_removed.doc: A bot's plugin was removed; its memory and transcript stay under its id (§6.1).

session_changed.doc: A session started, changed state or ended.

routines_changed.doc: The routine list changed; clients re-read `routine.list`.

agent_message.doc: A background agent's message to its bot.

routine_result.doc: A routine run's result in the main conversation.

note.doc: A labelled note in the conversation.

plugin_message.doc: A plugin's message to the bot; the turn it starts is the plugin's.
